# `Q-2-3` — Key-value Pair Before Class Specifier in Attribute

> Inside `{...}` attribute braces, a class specifier (`.name`)
> appears after a key-value pair (`key=value`).

## What this means

The attribute specifier syntax requires a specific order: the
identifier (`#id`) and class specifiers (`.class`) come first,
and key-value pairs (`key=value`) follow. This error fires when
a class specifier appears after at least one key-value pair has
already been parsed.

The constraint matches Pandoc's behavior and keeps the visual
ordering of attributes consistent: identity, classes, then
configuration.

## Why this happens

Usually a hand-written attribute that listed classes after
configuration by accident — or a programmatically-generated
attribute that assembled the pieces in the wrong order.

## How to fix

Reorder the attribute so all classes come before any key-value
pairs:

```markdown
[foo]{#id .class key=value}    <!-- correct -->
[foo]{#id key=value .class}    <!-- triggers Q-2-3 -->
```

## Example

The parser flags this input:

```markdown
[foo]{#id key=value .class}
```
